posts.title: Brake fluid: what it does and when to change it
posts.body:
Brake fluid carries the force from your pedal to the brakes. It slowly absorbs water from the air through the hoses and the reservoir cap. Water lowers the fluid's boiling point, so after a long downhill run or hard braking the fluid can boil and the pedal goes soft or long. Water also corrodes the lines, calipers and ABS parts from the inside.

What to check: the reservoir is a small translucent tank at the back of the engine bay, usually with a yellow or black cap. The level should sit between MIN and MAX. New fluid is clear to light amber; dark brown fluid is due. A level that keeps dropping means a leak or very worn pads, so have it looked at soon.

When to change it: most manufacturers say every two to three years regardless of mileage, and some test it at every service instead. A shop can measure the water content or boiling point in a minute. Use the type your owner's manual names (DOT 3, DOT 4 or DOT 5.1; DOT 5 silicone fluid is not interchangeable) and never top up with the wrong one.

Cost: a flush and bleed is usually a one-hour job. Expect roughly $80 to $150 in the US, £40 to £80 in the UK, CA$100 to CA$180 in Canada and A$100 to A$180 in Australia, more at dealers. Doing it yourself needs a helper or a one-person bleeder kit and a safe way to catch the old fluid; it eats paint, so wipe up spills at once.

Log the change in Checkpit with the date and mileage and set a reminder for two years, so the next one isn't forgotten.

posts.title: Does your car need a yearly inspection? US, UK, Canada and Australia
posts.body:
Whether your car needs a regular roadworthiness test depends on where it is registered. The rules below are the general picture; your local authority's website has the exact dates and fees.

United Kingdom: the MOT is required every year once a car is three years old (four in Northern Ireland). It covers brakes, tyres, lights, steering, suspension, emissions, the body and more. You can test up to a month minus a day before the current certificate expires and keep the same renewal date. Driving without a valid MOT can bring a fine and can void your insurance. The result and any advisories go into the free GOV.UK MOT history service.

United States: there is no federal test. Some states require an annual or two-yearly safety inspection, some only an emissions test in certain counties, and some have none at all. Your state's DMV or motor vehicle agency lists what applies and where.

Canada: rules are set by the provinces. Most do not require a periodic test for private cars, but several require a safety inspection when a car changes hands or comes in from another province, and some have emissions programs for older vehicles.

Australia: rules are set by the states. New South Wales needs an annual safety check (the pink slip) for most cars over five years old before registration renewal. Victoria needs a roadworthy certificate when a car is sold or re-registered, not every year. Queensland needs a safety certificate at sale. Other states have their own mixes.

Whatever applies to you, the things that fail most often are the same everywhere: tyres below the legal tread depth, lights out, worn brakes and wipers, and warning lights on the dash. A ten-minute look over the car the week before saves a retest. Put the due date in Checkpit as a reminder so the renewal doesn't catch you out.

posts.title: Toyota Camry (2018 and newer): maintenance guide
posts.body:
The Camry has a reputation for going a very long way with ordinary care. Here is the general maintenance picture for the 2018 and newer generation (2.5-litre four-cylinder, 3.5-litre V6 and the 2.5 hybrid). Older Camrys follow a similar pattern with shorter intervals. Your owner's manual is the final word.

Oil and filter: Toyota's North American schedule calls for 0W-20 full synthetic every 10,000 miles or 12 months, with a check and tyre rotation every 5,000 miles. Many owners shorten that to 5,000 to 7,500 miles if the car does a lot of short trips, towing or hot weather. Australian schedules are typically every 15,000 km or 12 months.

Other items: engine air filter around 30,000 miles (48,000 km); cabin filter yearly or so; spark plugs are iridium and last about 120,000 miles (190,000 km); coolant first at about 100,000 miles, then every 50,000; brake fluid every two to three years. The automatic transmission has no dipstick and Toyota lists its fluid as inspect only, but many independent shops suggest a drain and fill around 60,000 miles for cars kept long term. Hybrids add inverter coolant at about 100,000 miles.

Things owners report: the 2018 to 2019 cars were among many Toyotas in the Denso low-pressure fuel pump recall, so check your VIN on the NHTSA or Toyota recall page if you have not. Brake and tyre wear can be uneven if rotations are skipped.

Typical costs in the US: an oil change $60 to $100, front pads and rotors $300 to $500, a set of tyres $500 to $900. Prices run higher in Canada and Australia; in the UK the Camry is rarer and parts can take longer.

Set the oil, rotation and brake fluid reminders in Checkpit from your last service and log each visit. A complete history is the Camry's best resale argument.

posts.title: Toyota RAV4 (2019 and newer): maintenance guide
posts.body:
The RAV4 is one of the easier vehicles to keep on schedule. This guide covers the fifth generation (2019 and newer): the 2.5-litre petrol, the hybrid and the plug-in Prime. Older RAV4s follow a similar pattern with different engines. Your owner's manual is the final word.

Oil and filter: Toyota's North American schedule is roughly every 10,000 miles or 12 months with a thin synthetic oil (0W-16 or 0W-20, as your manual specifies). Short trips, towing, dust and very hot or cold weather count as severe use, so many owners change it at 5,000 to 7,500 miles. Other markets often use 15,000 km or 12 months. Rotate the tyres about every 5,000 to 7,500 miles.

Other items: engine air filter roughly every 30,000 miles (48,000 km), sooner on dusty roads; cabin filter about once a year; brake fluid every two to three years; coolant first at around 100,000 miles, then about every 50,000. All-wheel-drive versions have extra drivetrain fluid (rear differential and a power transfer unit) that your manual lists, and many shops change it between 30,000 and 60,000 miles if you tow or drive on loose surfaces.

Hybrid and Prime: the hybrid has its own inverter coolant loop and usually wears brake pads slowly because the motor does part of the braking, so judge pads by looking at them, not by mileage. The 12-volt battery still fails every few years and can leave the car dead. Prime owners should keep the charging port and cable clean and dry.

Recalls: check your VIN on the NHTSA or Toyota recall page (Transport Canada, GOV.UK or the Australian recalls site elsewhere).

Typical costs in the US, very roughly: an oil change $60 to $100, front pads and rotors $300 to $550, a set of tyres $600 to $1,000. Prices run higher in Canada and Australia and a little higher at dealers.

Set the oil, rotation and brake fluid reminders in Checkpit from your last service and log each visit. A complete history helps resale.

posts.title: Ford F-150 (2015 and newer): maintenance guide
posts.body:
The F-150 comes with many engine and drivetrain combinations, so this is a general picture for the 2015 and newer trucks (2.7- and 3.5-litre EcoBoost, 5.0-litre V8, 3.3-litre V6 and the PowerBoost hybrid). Your owner's manual and the truck's oil-life monitor are the final word.

Oil and filter: Ford's oil-life monitor sets the interval. Expect roughly 5,000 to 10,000 miles depending on how you drive, and sooner if you tow, idle a lot or make short trips. Use the grade in your manual (usually a 5W-20, 5W-30 or 0W-20 full synthetic). A truck holds more oil than a car, so a change costs more. Rotate the tyres about every 5,000 to 7,500 miles and set pressures from the sticker in the door jamb, higher when carrying or towing a load.

Towing and hauling: Ford's severe-duty schedule applies. Automatic transmission fluid, front and rear axle fluid and, on 4x4s, transfer case fluid are the items to shorten. Many owners who tow regularly change them every 30,000 to 60,000 miles, but follow the severe-duty list in your manual.

Other items: engine and cabin air filters about once a year, sooner on dusty roads; brake fluid every two to three years; coolant roughly every 100,000 miles for the first change, per the manual; the 12-volt battery lasts about three to five years. Turbocharged EcoBoost engines are harder on spark plugs, so do not stretch them beyond the manual's interval, especially if you tow. On a heavy truck, look at the brake pads at every rotation.

Recalls: check your VIN on the NHTSA or Ford recall page, or Transport Canada in Canada. The F-150 is sold mainly in the US, Canada and Mexico.

Typical costs in the US, very roughly: an oil change $70 to $130, front pads and rotors $300 to $600, a set of tyres $800 to $1,500. Canada runs a bit higher.

Set the oil, rotation and brake fluid reminders in Checkpit from your last service and log each visit. A complete history helps resale.

posts.title: Honda CR-V (2017 and newer): maintenance guide
posts.body:
The CR-V is known for low running costs. This guide covers the fifth generation (2017 to 2022) and the sixth (2023 and newer): the 1.5-litre turbo, the 2.4-litre petrol on early cars and the 2.0-litre hybrid. Your owner's manual is the final word.

The Maintenance Minder: instead of a fixed mileage, Honda's dashboard shows a code when service is due. A and B mean engine oil (B adds the filter and a round of inspections), and the numbers are extra items such as tyre rotation, air filters, transmission fluid, spark plugs and coolant. Look the codes up in the manual or on Honda's website, and do not ignore a code because it seems early.

Oil and filter: use the grade in your manual (a 0W-20 full synthetic is the usual one). The Minder commonly asks for an oil change somewhere between 5,000 and 10,000 miles depending on use. Turbo engines like short winter trips least, so check the dipstick level now and then.

Other items: rotate the tyres about every 5,000 to 7,500 miles; cabin filter about once a year; engine air filter roughly every 15,000 to 30,000 miles; brake fluid every three years or as the Minder says. Cars with a continuously variable transmission (CVT) need Honda's own CVT fluid, never a generic one, and the Minder tells you when. All-wheel-drive versions also have rear differential fluid. On the hybrid, pads often last longer because the motor helps with braking.

Recalls: check your VIN on the NHTSA or Honda recall page, or Transport Canada, GOV.UK or the Australian recalls site.

Typical costs in the US, very roughly: an oil change $60 to $100, a CVT fluid service $150 to $300, front pads and rotors $300 to $550, a set of tyres $600 to $1,000. Canada and Australia run higher.

Set the oil, rotation and brake fluid reminders in Checkpit from your last service and log each visit. A complete history helps resale.
